ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.12 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexcused second deviation (F4); the first deviation (F3) stands as agreed. No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI trip Hougang Mall → VivoCity, metered, $47.80 charged [F8]. Two off-route segments exist, so each is reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 (12:49–12:55, +1.31 km): the driver messaged at 12:46 "Jam on Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 is building up ahead, can I go round via Serangoon Garden Way?" [F9] and the rider replied at 12:47 "Sure, go ahead." [F10] — a rider message, timestamped (the chat record is complete, every message timestamped [F11]), sent before the segment started at 12:49. Read in context this is a rider agreement to a specific named area, Serangoon Garden Way, and the timing plus the driver's question tie the first turn-off to that jam-avoidance route; the record places nothing for this segment elsewhere. The agreement covers the first deviation, so it is not treated as a detour [F9][F10][RD-5]. The RD-4 incident screen fails (no traffic incident, speed band alone does not exempt) [F14][F15][RD-4], and no rider-named stop was measured [F3][RD-3], both of which are settled by the trace.

Segment F4 (13:07–13:13, +2.21 km to 1239 m off the optimal route): this second turn-off happened 20 minutes after the rider's only message; there is no rider message before 13:07 agreeing to it [F9][F10][F11]. The only explanation is the driver's own post-trip statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" [F12] — a driver statement, not rider consent, and no rider message supports it (G11) [RD-5]. The rider's complaint confirms this reading: she agreed to "go round the jam near the start, but later he went off the route a second time without asking". F4 is therefore an unexcused deviation and is refundable [F4][RD-2].

Amount: rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = $1.4099/km (the figure the trace states) [F8]. Refund only the non-exempt segment's extra km: 2.21 km × $1.4099/km = $3.1159 → $3.12 [F4][F8][RD-2]. F3's 1.31 km and F5's whole-trip excess are not refunded because that segment was agreed [F3][F5][RD-5]. The waiting charge is a meter waiting unit, not refundable [F6][RD-3].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make him a repeated route offender and no account flag issues; profile facts cannot decide the case anyway [F18][RD-6]. The rider's own 0 upheld disputes are irrelevant to the merits [F17].
